title: Room 39 - The Sealed Bunker Under The Kremlin

target.note: short declaratives, one idea per beat. Little to no pause between sentences.

narration:
Under the Kremlin, a nuclear bunker waits.
Nobody has ever walked through its door.
Its code name is Object 739.
Stalin ordered it built in the 1950s.
He wanted one refuge of his own.
It sits below a small park.
Moscow itself was built on sinking ground.
Everything above the ceiling is hardened steel.
Ordinary buildings nearby rest on thin foundations.
The doors were made to close forever.
Each leaf weighs hundreds of tonnes.
They are sealed, and never opened.
One closed door, filling the whole frame.
Stalin reportedly never went inside.
The corridors were lined with lead.
Floor to ceiling, plate over plate.
Below that, a control room waits.
The room is said to hold one console.
A console drawn small, in the dark.
One row of switches, one big button.
No official record confirms the console.
Other bunkers from that era were documented.
This one has never been filmed inside.
Satellite images show only the surface.
The entrance sits behind an ordinary fence.
An ordinary fence on an ordinary street.
It ends at a set of steel doors.
Rumour says they open on a code.
No code has ever been published.
The whole site is a system.
A line of sensors ringing the block.
Something out there is still listening.
The system may have outlived its builder.
Under the park, a red light waits.
Russia has never confirmed what remains.
No one has gone down in decades.
The door is still shut, and still waiting.

beats.line: It sits below a small park.

beats.line: Moscow itself was built on sinking ground.

beats.line: Everything above the ceiling is hardened steel.
beats.visual: armoured ceiling slab, riveted, drawn very thick; character standing on it for scale

beats.line: Ordinary buildings nearby rest on thin foundations.
beats.visual: a thin ordinary basement wall beside it, hand-lettered label 'ABOVE' vs 'BELOW'

beats.line: The doors were made to close forever.

beats.line: Each leaf weighs hundreds of tonnes.

beats.line: They are sealed, and never opened.
beats.visual: weld seam drawn across the door edge, bright and uneven, sealing it shut

beats.line: One closed door, filling the whole frame.
beats.visual: the closed door held dead centre, filling the whole frame, nothing else in shot

beats.line: Stalin reportedly never went inside.
beats.visual: character shrugging at a desk; speech bubble 'he never went in'

beats.line: The corridors were lined with lead.
beats.visual: cutaway corridor cross-section, thick dark plates on floor, walls and ceiling

beats.line: Floor to ceiling, plate over plate.
beats.visual: the plates drawn edge to edge, one long continuous band; label 'LEAD LINED'

beats.line: Below that, a control room waits.
beats.visual: one low chamber at the end of the corridor, single light above it; character tiny, awed

beats.line: The room is said to hold one console.
beats.visual: cutaway of the chamber, a blocky console shape under a hanging lamp; label 'SAID TO EXIST'

beats.line: A console drawn small, in the dark.
beats.visual: the console alone in a wide dark room, one small warm pool of light

beats.line: One row of switches, one big button.
beats.visual: close on one row of switches and one large red button under a hinged cover

beats.line: No official record confirms the console.
beats.visual: character deadpan beside an empty file folder; speech bubble 'no record'

beats.line: Other bunkers from that era were documented.
beats.visual: another bunker from the same decade, open to visitors, a queue of small figures

beats.line: This one has never been filmed inside.
beats.visual: our bunker door beside it, the visitor line cut off at the edge

beats.line: Satellite images show only the surface.
beats.visual: satellite passing overhead looking straight down; only rooftops and trees visible

beats.line: The entrance sits behind an ordinary fence.
beats.visual: ordinary grey perimeter fence on an ordinary street, parked cars behind it

beats.line: An ordinary fence on an ordinary street.
beats.visual: the same fence held from further back, trees, a bench, a bus stop

beats.line: It ends at a set of steel doors.
beats.visual: the fence line running to a plain steel door set into a brick wall; label 'ENTRANCE'

beats.line: Rumour says they open on a code.
beats.visual: a keypad and a small camera on a stalk above the steel door

beats.line: No code has ever been published.
beats.visual: the keypad close, no numbers legible, a blank panel of twelve unmarked buttons

beats.line: The whole site is a system.
beats.visual: the whole block drawn as a system: fence, sensors, door, chamber, all linked by one dashed line

beats.line: A line of sensors ringing the block.
beats.visual: a ring of small sensor boxes around the block, each with a short antenna

beats.line: Something out there is still listening.
beats.visual: one sensor box close, a small red lamp lit on its face

beats.line: The system may have outlived its builder.
beats.visual: the block's outline dissolving into rust and weeds; the dashed line still runs through it

beats.line: Under the park, a red light waits.
beats.visual: the park at night, cutaway, a small red glow in the chamber below; no label

beats.line: Russia has never confirmed what remains.
beats.visual: an official document on a desk, the relevant line left blank and unmarked

beats.line: No one has gone down in decades.
beats.visual: the chamber dark, an empty helmet on a chair, nothing moving

beats.line: The door is still shut, and still waiting.
beats.visual: the steel door held in near-darkness, a red lamp beside it; character small, seen from behind, waiting; no label
